newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amnesty welcomes release of Jordanian dissident.
newsitem.headline: Amnesty welcomes release of Jordanian dissident.

text.p: The human rights group Amnesty International has welcomed the release of Jordanian dissident Laith Shubailat and urged the government to free all remaining political prisoners under an amnesty announced last week.

The organisation said in a statement received on Tuesday it considered Shubailat a prisoner of conscience "detained solely because of his opposition to (Jordan's) peace agreement with Israel and his other peaceful political activities."

Shubailat, leader of Jordan's Islamist-dominated engineers' union and a vocal critic of King Hussein's 1994 peace treaty with Israel, was released on November 8 after serving eight months of a three-year sentence. He had accused the monarch of treason over the peace accord.
King Hussein drove to Swaqa prison, 80 km (50 miles) south of Amman to inform Shubailat of his release, and then drove him home to his mother.

The king later declared a general amnesty for detainees arrested in connection with widespread bread riots in August and for other prisoners not considered a threat to public security or whose time in prison was deemed sufficient punishment.

"Amnesty International welcomes the release of Laith Shubailat," the organisation said. It urged the government to include in the general amnesty "all other prisoners held solely for the non-violent expression of their conscientiously-held beliefs."

It said 253 people might be eligible for pardon under the bread riot amnesty. Government officials say up to 1,200 cases will be reviewed by a judicial panel charged with carrying out the broader amnesty.
